([[Malvern, Pennsylvania]]) | college = [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] (2024–2025) | highlights = * [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Sixth Man of the Year (2025) }} '''William Riley''' (born February 10, 2006) is a Canadian [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois Fighting Illini]]. ==High school career== Riley attended high school at Southwest Academy Prep in [[London, Ontario]] with brief stops at [[Preston High School (Ontario)|Preston High School]] and [[Grand River Collegiate Institute]].{{cite web |last=Bryson |first=Mark |title=Kitchener's Will Riley hot in pursuit of NBA dream |url=https://www.therecord.com/sports/basketball/kitcheners-will-riley-hot-in-pursuit-of-nba-dream/article_3de361ba-23aa-53d9-882f-609ab80f648c.html |website=The Record |access-date=23 September 2024 |date=2 March 2024}} He then attended [[The Phelps School]] in [[Malvern, PA]] where he spent the last two years of his high school career. He was ranked as the top-ranked Canadian prospect and No. 9 overall by [[247Sports]], No. 10 by [[On3.com]], and No. 11 by [[Rivals.com]] in the class of 2025. He averaged 21.9 points, 4.7 rebounds, and 2.5 assists during [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League|EYBL]] and was named Offensive MVP of the EYBL Indy Session, starring for UPlay Canada.{{cite web |title=Riley Signs with Illinois |url=https://fightingillini.com/news/2024/6/23/mens-basketball-riley-signs-with-illinois.aspx |website=University of Illinois Athletics |access-date=23 September 2024 |language=en |date=23 June 2024}} He was named MVP of the 2024 [[Basketball Without Borders]] Global Camp during [[NBA All-Star weekend]].{{cite web |title=Canadian Will Riley named MVP of BWB Global camp |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/news/canadian-will-riley-named-mvp-of-bwb-global-camp |website=FIBA.basketball |date=19 February 2024 |access-date=23 September 2024 |language=en}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|collapse=no|year=2024}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Will Riley | position = F | hometown = [[Kitchener, Ontario]] | highschool = [[The Phelps School]] | feet = 6 | inches = 8 | weight = 180 | 40 = | commitdate = 6/23/24 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn rank = | espn stars = 5 | grayshirt = | On3 stars = 5 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2024 | rivals ref title = 2024 Illinois Commits | scout ref title = Men's Basketball Recruiting | espn ref title = ESPN- Illinois Fighting Illini Men's Basketball Recruiting | rivals school = illinois | 247 school = illinois | scout s = | espn schoolid = 356 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 11 | espn overall = | 247 overall = 10 | accessdate = | bball = yes |On3 overall = 20 |On3 school = illinois-fighting-illini }} ==College career== On June 23, 2024, Riley committed to [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]]. He was originally part of the class of 2025 but reclassified to 2024 to join earlier. At the time of his signing, Riley was the highest-ranked recruit signed by [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]] in the internet era, surpassing [[Dee Brown (basketball, born 1984)|Dee Brown]] from the class of 2002. ===Freshman season=== On Monday, November 11th, 2024, Riley was named the first [[2024–25 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season#Players of the week|Big Ten Freshman of the Week for the 2024-25 season]]. Riley's overall week (averaging 22.5 points and 7.0 rebounds per game) in two Illinois wins, as well as his securing the Illini freshman scoring record, tipped the scales in his favor.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/illinois/basketball/will-riley-big-ten-freshman-of-the-week-illinois |title=Illinois Guard Will Riley Named Big Ten Freshman of the Week|date=11 November 2024 }} He went on to receive the award twice more.{{cite web|url=https://fightingillini.com/news/2025/2/10/mens-basketball-riley-nabs-third-b1g-freshman-of-the-week-accolade.aspx |title=Riley Nabs Third B1G Freshman of the Week Accolade |date=10 February 2025 }} Following the Big Ten regular season's conclusion, he was named Big Ten Sixth Man of the Year.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/illinois/article/will-riley-big-ten-freshman-of-the-year-illinois-fighting-illini-basketball-246835400/ |title=Illini freshman Will Riley wins Big Ten Sixth Man of the Year }} He later declared for the [[2025 NBA Draft]],{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/44673022/illinois-riley-projected-1st-rounder-enters-nba-draft |title=Illini's Riley, projected 1st-rounder, enters draft |date=14 April 2025 }} and received a green room invite in the second wave of invitations on June 16.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/45525667/six-more-players-receive-nba-draft-green-room-invites |title=Sources: Six more receive NBA green room invites }} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] | 35 || 9 || 25.7 || .432 || .326 || .724 || 4.1 || 2.2 || 0.2 || 0.2 || 12.6 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Riley's parents are named Ray and Tracy ({{nee|Hooks}}). His parents both played sports in high school.
